quote: I desire you would Remember the Ladies, and be more generous and favourable to them than your ancestors.
source: Abigail Adams, letter to John Adams, Braintree, 31 March to 5 April 1776 (Adams Family Correspondence, Massachusetts Historical Society)

evidence.where: the Massachusetts Historical Society transcript of the manuscript letter, read against the proposal
evidence.edition: Adams Family Correspondence, Massachusetts Historical Society, Adams Papers digital edition
evidence.locator: Letter from Abigail Adams to John Adams, 31 March to 5 April 1776, headed Braintree March 31, 1776, in the portion written on 31 March

reason: The transcript reads and by the way in the new Code of Laws which I suppose it will be necessary for you to make I desire you would Remember the Ladies, and be more generous and favourable to them than your ancestors. The lift begins at a clause and ends where the sentence ends, so the capital I and the full stop are the manuscript’s own, and the capitals on Remember and Ladies are kept. The Society itself heads the document 31 March to 5 April 1776. Abigail Adams stands at two for the year, so this is her third and last line.
